name: Peyaji
subtitle: crisp onion fritters shot through with nigella and green chilli

ingredients.qty: 4 medium (about 400g), sliced as thin as you can

ingredients.note: this is what makes them stay crisp

prepNotes: Slice the onions along the grain into long thin strips — rings fall apart in the oil.
Salt the sliced onions and leave 15 minutes; they will release enough water that you need almost none extra.
Mix the batter only 2 minutes before frying, or the onions weep and it turns soupy.

steps.text: Squeeze the salted onions lightly with your hands to bring out their water, keeping the liquid in the bowl.
steps.tip: That onion water is your only liquid. Do not throw it away and do not add tap water.

steps.text: Add the besan, rice flour, nigella, green chilli, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander leaves and mix with your fingers.
The mixture should just cling together in a ragged clump — add 1 tsp water at a time only if it is genuinely dry.
steps.tip: A loose batter gives you a pancake instead of a fritter. Err on the dry side.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then bring it down to a steady 170C.
Drop in irregular clumps the size of a walnut, six or seven at a time.
steps.tip: Craggy shapes fry crisper than neat balls. Do not pat them smooth.

steps.text: Fry 4-5 minutes, turning once at the halfway point, until deep amber and no longer bubbling hard.
steps.tip: The bubbling slowing down tells you the moisture has cooked out and they will be crisp.

steps.text: Lift onto a wire rack, not paper, so the undersides stay crisp.
Fry the next batch, letting the oil come back up to temperature between batches, and serve hot with rice and dal or on their own with mustard.

storage: Best within 30 minutes of frying. Leftovers can be re-crisped in a hot oven for 5 minutes but never in a microwave.
